svg.text: Supported Field Deployment Topologies: Cabin Nearby vs. Remote / Obstacle Crossing
Identical camera node hardware supports direct fiber to a cabin (up to 10 km), a buried Dead-Drop Vault, or a COTS optical beam.
SCENARIO A: CABIN OR OUTBUILDING SOMEWHAT CLOSE BY (30 m to 10 km)
Solution: Simply use a longer pre-terminated OS2 fiber spool!
1. Tree Split-Pod Camera Node
• Micro Pod (2m up tree) + Buried Vault
• Media Converter #1 TX (1310nm, -3 dBm)
• 1x2 Splitter Out 1 -> Local RX Loopback
• 1x2 Splitter Out 2 -> Outbound Fiber (-6.8 dBm)
2. Moss-Buried 3mm Armored OS2 Fiber
• Simply plug in 50m, 300m, 1km, or 10km spool
• 1310nm single-mode loss is only 0.35 dB/km!
• +13.2 dB link margin = >10 km with ZERO repeaters
• Tucked 2cm under moss; 100% snow/fog immune
3. Indoor Cabin Collector Hub
• Media Converter #2 (RX connected; TX capped)
• Cat6 RJ45 -> Cabin Mac / Linux / Pi Hub
• Runs receiver_hub.py + dashboard_server.py
• Real-time verified JPEGs + local alerts
SC/UPC
1310nm Light
SCENARIO B: NO CABIN NEARBY — OR CROSSING A RIVER / STRAIT / PUBLIC ROAD
Three Practical COTS Modes (Fiber Vault, Water FSO & 20km Troposcatter)
MODE B1: No Cabin Nearby -> Buried 'Dead-Drop' Collector Vault (100m–500m in Woods)
• How It Works: Run 100m–300m of 3mm armored fiber under the moss from the Tree Camera Node
deep into the forest (away from the trail/road) to a 2nd buried waterproof QILIPSU vault.
• Inside the Dead-Drop Vault: Media Converter #2 (RX) + Headless Pi / SSD + 12V Battery
running `receiver_hub.py --max-alerts 1000` (circular disk cap).
• Why This Beats On-Camera SD Storage: Even if a burglar spots and destroys the camera,
the signed high-res JPEGs were already transmitted at light speed 200m away into the hidden vault!
• Retrieval / Optional Remote Uplink: Extract via `receiver_hub.py --export-bundle alerts.zip`
OR attach `sky-diode-relay` Build D (200m–20km Troposcatter) to the Vault 200m away (camera stays 0.00W RF!).
MODE B2: River / Strait / Road Crossing -> COTS Free-Space Optical (FSO) Beam
• When to Use: A river, Saimaa water strait, or paved road blocks laying a 3mm fiber cable.
• Can We Buy a Cheap Existing Beam System? YES — Two COTS Options (Zero Custom Soldering):
1. Plug-and-Play Fiber Collimators on Existing Media Converters ($200–$280 pair, 5m–80m LOS):
Screw two US-made Thorlabs (F220FC-1310 / F280FC-C) or Edmund Optics SC/FC collimators
directly onto Converter #1 TX and Converter #2 RX! Mount on rigid low bedrock/ground stakes
(never high on a swaying tree). Shoots an invisible 1310nm 1 Gbps laser beam across the gap.
2. Industrial IP67 Optical Data Transceivers (Leuze DDLS 200 / Sick ISD400, Made in Germany):
Turnkey 100 Mbps Ethernet optical beam (100m–500m range, wide beam tolerance; ~$250–$450 surplus).
MODE B3 (Ordered Build D — 10-Line COTS BOM): 200 m – 20 km All-Weather 2.4 GHz Troposcatter & Canopy-Bounce (`sky-diode-relay`)
• Zero-trenching 200m–20km over-the-hill NLOS link: ADALM-PLUTO SDRs + Skyworks SE2576L 1W PA + SKY65405 1.2dB NF LNA + VBF-2435+ Filters + 14dBi Panels.
• Bounces VK7MO lock-in frames (+55.8 dB gain) off tropospheric turbulence, rain/snow clouds & forest canopies (+14.1 dB to +62.3 dB SNR across all seasons).
• 6-Layer Electronic Anti-Jamming: Hops into 2380/2488 MHz out-of-ISM guard bands outside Wi-Fi/drone jammers + MAD barrage rejection (23/23 tests pass).
